passage: The collection of rare maps in the university library ______ several that were drawn by hand in the sixteenth century, long before modern surveying tools were available to mapmakers.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
To pick a verb, first find the real subject. It's often hiding in front of a phrase that starts with "of" or "in."

Here the subject is "the collection." "Of rare maps" and "in the university library" just describe it. Cross them out in your head: "The collection ______ several..."

One collection, so the verb is singular: "includes."

rationales.A: "Include" matches "maps," but "maps" sits inside "of rare maps" and isn't the subject. The subject is the single collection.
rationales.C: "Are including" is plural, but the subject, "collection," is singular.
rationales.D: "Have included" is plural, but the subject, "collection," is singular.

passage: In 1969, after years of planning and testing, the city ______ its first underground subway line, which carried more than fifty thousand passengers on its very first day of service.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
Look for time clues. "In 1969" places this at a specific moment in the past, and the sentence later says the line "carried" passengers, also past.

So the verb should be simple past: "opened."

rationales.A: "Opens" is present tense, but this happened in 1969.
rationales.B: "Will open" is future tense, but this is in the past.
rationales.C: "Has opened" doesn't go with a specific past date like "In 1969." Use the simple past instead.

passage: When the students in Ms. Ruiz's biology class finished building a model of the human heart, ______ displayed it in the school's front hallway so that visitors could see how blood moves through the heart's four chambers.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
A pronoun has to match the noun it stands for. Ask: who displayed the model? The students did.

"Students" is plural, so the pronoun must be plural: "they."

rationales.B: "It" is singular and would seem to mean the model, which can't display itself.
rationales.C: "He or she" is for one person, but there are many students.
rationales.D: "One" is a vague, general pronoun that doesn't clearly point to the students.

passage: Each spring, the community garden on Elm Street holds a plant sale to raise money. This year, the ______ proceeds will be used to buy new gardening tools and to build a small shed for storing them.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
The proceeds belong to something, so you need a possessive. The question is singular or plural.

The text describes "a plant sale," just one. For one owner, add an apostrophe and s: "sale's."

Quick rule: one owner gets 's; plural owners ending in s get just an apostrophe after the s.

rationales.A: "Sales" is a plain plural. Without an apostrophe it doesn't show ownership.
rationales.B: "Sales'" means the proceeds of several sales, but there's only one sale.

passage: The paintings in the gallery's east wing, which were donated by a local collector in the 1950s, ______ some of the earliest known landscapes created by artists from the region.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
The subject is buried under a lot of extra words. Peel them away: "in the gallery's east wing" describes the paintings, and "which were donated by a local collector in the 1950s" is a side note.

What's left: "The paintings ______ some of the earliest known landscapes."

"Paintings" is plural, so the verb is "are."

rationales.A: "Is" is singular. It might sound right next to "wing" or "collector," but the subject is "paintings."
rationales.C: "Was" is singular, and it also switches to past tense.
rationales.D: "Has been" is singular, but "paintings" is plural.

passage: Having studied the ruins near the river for more than a decade, combining careful ground surveys with aerial photographs taken in different seasons of the year, ______
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: the ancient city's layout was finally understood by the archaeologist.
the archaeologist's understanding of the ancient city's layout was finally complete.
the ancient city finally revealed its layout to the archaeologist.
the archaeologist finally understood the layout of the ancient city.
explanation:
The sentence opens with a description, "Having studied the ruins near the river for more than a decade..." That describes someone who did the studying.

Whatever comes right after the comma is the one doing that studying. It has to be a person, so it must be "the archaeologist."

Choice D puts the archaeologist right after the comma. The others put the city, the layout or an "understanding" there, which would mean those things studied the ruins.

rationales.A: This makes the city's layout the one that studied the ruins, which doesn't make sense.
rationales.B: This makes "the archaeologist's understanding" the one that studied the ruins. The person needs to come first, not their understanding.
rationales.C: This makes the ancient city the one that studied the ruins.

passage: Among the artifacts recovered from the shipwreck ______ a bronze navigational instrument and a set of clay jars that were still sealed with wax when divers brought them to the surface.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
This sentence is flipped: the verb comes before the subject. Turn it around to see it clearly: "A bronze instrument and a set of clay jars ______ among the artifacts."

The subject is two things joined by "and," which makes it plural. Plural subject, plural verb: "were."

rationales.B: "Was" is singular. It might sound right next to "a bronze navigational instrument," but the subject includes the jars too.
rationales.C: "Has been" is singular, but the subject is two things.
rationales.D: "Is" is singular and also switches to present tense.

passage: By the time the expedition finally reached the summit, the weather ______ dramatically: the clear skies of the early morning had given way to heavy snow and strong winds.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
Two past moments are in play. The expedition reached the summit, and before that, the weather changed.

When one past event happened before another past event, use "had" for the earlier one: "had changed." The sentence even models it later with "had given way."

rationales.A: "Changes" is present tense, but everything here is in the past.
rationales.B: "Has changed" connects the past to now. Here you need something earlier than another past moment.
rationales.D: "Will have changed" is future, but the expedition has already reached the summit.

passage: Many of the letters ______ by the poet during her travels through southern Europe were never published, but historians have recently located several of them in a private family collection.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation:
The sentence already has its main verb: "were never published." So the blank isn't a main verb; it's a word describing the letters.

The letters didn't do any writing; they were written by the poet. Describing something that received an action calls for "written."

Read it back: "Many of the letters written by the poet ... were never published." It flows.

rationales.A: "Writing" would mean the letters were doing the writing.
rationales.C: "Wrote" is a main verb, so the sentence would have two competing verbs, and it would make the letters the writers.
rationales.D: "Had written" is a full verb that clashes with "were," and it would make the letters the writers.
